claims.text: A hybrid framework combining ab initio electronic calculations with Green–Kubo methods can separately predict electronic and lattice thermal conductivity.
The hybrid framework can achieve approximately 10–15% accuracy for oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr over 200–1200 K.
Up to 1 wt.% oxygen represents a realistic defect concentration in HfNbTaTiZr.
Ab initio calculations can determine the mode-dependent electronic properties needed by the proposed framework.
Green–Kubo molecular dynamics with machine-learned force fields can simulate phonon transport in oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr supercells.
Oxygen doping produces atomic-scale defect scattering and heterogeneous local environments in HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical fluctuations, lattice distortion, and strain fluctuations in high-entropy materials strengthen phonon scattering and reduce lattice thermal conductivity.
Both lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions are significant and distinguishable throughout 200–1200 K in 1 wt.% oxygen HfNbTaTiZr.
Computing electronic transport from ab initio electronic states and lattice transport with Green–Kubo time correlations explicitly decouples electron and phonon transport.
The proposed framework avoids requiring an averaged Debye temperature.
Explicit oxygen-containing supercells better capture defect-induced scattering and chemical complexity than averaged-parameter approaches.
The predicted total thermal conductivity should remain within ±10–15% of experiment across 200–1200 K.
The method should identify a change in the relative lattice and electronic contributions near 200 K that matches experiment.
Earlier defect-free or channel-conflating models typically deviate from experiment by more than 15%.
Ideal-crystal and Debye-based assumptions are responsible for the poorer agreement of earlier models.
The framework is applicable to oxygen-doped HfNbTaTiZr from 200 to 1200 K.
Its accuracy may diminish well below 200 K or when the sample has substantially different defect concentrations.
Mode-specific scattering and nonlinear interactions between electronic and phononic scattering channels are important unresolved uncertainties.
Inelastic neutron scattering or time-domain thermoreflectance under variable magnetic fields can independently isolate the lattice thermal conductivity in this alloy.
Electronic thermal conductivity can be independently obtained from electrical conductivity and Lorenz-number measurements using Wiedemann–Franz analysis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts and requires testing a crossover described as occurring below approximately 200 K, but the stated validity range and proposed measurements begin at 200 K, so the experiment cannot decisively test a below-200 K crossover.

The initial-state field allows oxygen contents up to 1 wt.%, whereas the conditions and validation experiment specify exactly 1 wt.%; the scope therefore shifts between a concentration range and a single composition.
